title: Seeing Is Locating: Spatial Awareness and Geographic Bias in Decision Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.30564v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Decision models, which output probability distributions over candidate labels instead of generating text, are increasingly used as classifiers and evaluators for inputs associated with real-world locations. However, it remains unclear whether they can leverage spatial context and whether their predictions are geographically biased. We introduce GeoDecisions, a multimodal benchmark for evaluating the spatial awareness and geographic bias of decision models. GeoDecisions comprises two tasks: (1) geo-aware image classification, and (2) location rating on objective and subjective topics. Evaluating six decision models against supervised task-specific models, we find that spatial awareness requires vision: textual coordinates alone provide insufficient context for classifying everyday photos and satellite images. translated_title: 眼见即定位：决策语言模型中的空间感知与地理偏见
translated_abstract: 决策模型输出的不是生成的文本，而是候选标签上的概率分布，它们越来越多地被用作与真实世界位置相关输入的分类器和评估器。然而，这些模型能否利用空间上下文，以及其预测是否存在地理偏见，目前仍不清楚。我们提出了 GeoDecisions，一个用于评估决策模型空间感知能力和地理偏见的多模态基准。GeoDecisions 包含两个任务：(1) 地理感知图像分类；(2) 针对客观与主观主题的位置评分。通过将六个决策模型与监督式的任务特定模型进行对比评估，我们发现空间感知需要视觉能力：仅凭文本坐标不足以提供对日常照片和卫星图像进行分类所需的上下文。我们还发现了显著的地理偏见。在日常照片上，尽管开源权重的决策模型取得了更高的准确率，但其表现出……
tldr: 决策语言模型需要视觉输入才能实现空间感知，且其预测存在显著的地理偏见。
en_tdlr: Decision language models require visual input to achieve spatial awareness, and their predictions exhibit substantial geographic bias.
